messages:
alex: Hey—ran into a weird redwoodctl auth/localserve mismatch after a brew install. I have a zsh plugin that sets XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$HOME/.config. I do `redwoodctl auth login` and it says success, but `redwoodctl local serve` fails with "rpc: unauthenticated". Repro: 1) brew install redwoodctl 2) export XDG_CONFIG_HOME=~/.config in zshrc 3) redwoodctl auth login 4) redwoodctl local serve --> fails. Anyone seen XDG vs legacy config dir weirdness?

maria: can you paste `redwoodctl version` and `echo "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME"`? also `ls -la ~/.redwood ~/.config/redwood`

alex: version: 2.3.1
$XDG_CONFIG_HOME -> /Users/alex/.config
ls ~/.config/redwood
  token  settings.json
ls ~/.redwood
  (no such file or directory)
So the token ended up in ~/.config/redwood/token, but redwoodctl local serve is apparently looking under ~/.redwood and failing to find it.

sam: two quick checks: `brew list --versions redwoodctl` (to rule out older binary) and `redwoodctl --help | grep config` — there should be an env var to override the dir. Also try `REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.config/redwood redwoodctl local serve` to force it.

alex: `brew list --versions redwoodctl` -> redwoodctl 2.3.1
Tried `REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.config/redwood redwoodctl local serve` and that works (local serve starts). So binary respects env override but not XDG env automatically.

jen: this smells like an installer/homebrew formula vs runtime mismatch: installer used XDG to write the token, but the shipped binary defaults to legacy ~/.redwood unless REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR is set. Workarounds: a) set REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR in shells, b) symlink `~/.config/redwood -> ~/.redwood`, c) run `redwoodctl auth login --config-dir ~/.redwood`. For quick unblocking try `ln -s ~/.config/redwood ~/.redwood`

alex: symlink fixed it: `ln -s ~/.config/redwood ~/.redwood` then `redwoodctl local serve` worked. Ugh. Will file a bug.

maria: please include minimal repro + output of `redwoodctl auth login` (it prints where it stores the token) and the contents of the homebrew postinstall script if any. If brew formula wrote the token, that'll help triage.

sam: opened a draft issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/1024 — title: "Config dir parity: homebrew installer writes XDG, binary looks at legacy ~/.redwood". Suggestion in issue: binary should check both XDG and legacy paths (in that order), and the installer should write to both locations for backward compatibility.

devex-bot: devex checklist idea: add a `redwoodctl doctor` command that prints which config dir the binary will read, what env vars are set, and where tokens exist. Also add a line to the macOS quickstart about XDG vs legacy config.

jen: agree on `doctor` + formula fix. I'll draft a small PR to homebrew to either remove the postinstall token write or set both locations. Trying to keep the CLI behavior stable is probably best.

alex: thanks all — leaving the symlink until we ship a fix. I'll paste the minimal repro into the issue and link to this thread. Also adding a short note to the onboarding doc so new hires with zsh plugins don't get blocked. :thumbsup:
